text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000001 bills 99215 well above expectation at every complexity level, including heavily on low-complexity patients, but records came back for too few 99215 claims to confirm or refute support.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern is consistent with upcoding. The excess 99215 share holds within every complexity band, not just the sicker ones. Nearly half the 99215s fall on patients with 0–1 conditions, and sampled examples such as C0000046, C0000099 and C0000354 carry acute or follow-up diagnoses like J06.9, Z09 and N39.0. The documentation points the other way but is thin: only 4 documented 99215s, all supported at high MDM. Two of those (C0000566 and C0000623) are low-complexity claims, and two of the four record no minutes. The 4 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence of note inflation, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 sample, prioritizing the Z09 and J06.9 visits, and check whether the high-MDM notes look templated or cloned across patients."}
